RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: Not reliably estimable from the information provided

An all-women panel is not, by itself, evidence of sex bias. Your longer experience and qualifications warrant meaningful feedback, but do not establish that you were the stronger candidate for a leadership role. Client relationships, staff management, commercial performance and interview results can legitimately matter.

Follow up in writing requesting the selection criteria, their weighting and feedback on your assessment. Two weeks’ silence is worth chasing, but is not evidence of discrimination.

Raise a discrimination concern if concrete indicators emerge—such as sex-based remarks, inconsistent criteria or different treatment—not simply because of the panel’s composition. If considering formal action, check local complaint deadlines promptly.
